description:
## Question

What are the candidate mechanisms for reducing a full build to only what a change affects, and what does each cost/guarantee?

Survey at least:
- **Path heuristics** — `git diff` → `packages/<name>/**` → build that package. Cheap, no eval; but blind to `lib/`, `flake.lock`, and toolchain meta-packages that depend on a bumped component.
- **Derivation-level diff** — evaluate `packages.<system>` on base and on head, compare `drvPath`/`outPath` per attribute, build the difference. Exact by construction. Cost = 2× full eval (see the baseline ticket).
- **Cache-query-based** — skip "what changed" entirely: evaluate once, then ask the substituter which out-paths it already has (narinfo `HEAD` / `nix path-info --store https://firefly-toolbox.cachix.org`) and build only the misses. Notably this *also* answers "is the cache pre-populated?" without downloading anything.
- **Off-the-shelf tooling** — `nix-eval-jobs`, `nix-fast-build`, `nixbuild.net`, `garnix`, DeterminateSystems magic-nix-cache, and any GitHub Action that already does base-vs-head flake diffing.

For each: exactness (false negatives?), eval cost, whether it needs a base checkout, whether it needs the cachix token, and how it handles this repo’s shape (nested versions, `symlinkJoin` toolchains, `legacyPackages` vs `packages`).

Deliver a comparison table as a linked markdown asset.
title: Survey: mechanisms for computing the set to build
